subject: Benchmark playbook transfer — Pioneer Health onboarding
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Claire Park <claire.park@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Handoff: Pioneer Health benchmark goals and initial artifacts

Hi Claire / Samir,

Looping Aditya in for the technical handoff on the Pioneer Health onboarding. Per our SOW the acceptance benchmark focuses on two measurable goals:
- Throughput: sustain 120 QPS at 95% success rate during 30-minute steady-state windows
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms server-side for generation requests (20–50 tokens response typical)

Attachments: I uploaded the initial load profile and recent trace captures to the shared Drive folder (link below). Samir — you already sent a small harness; I've attached the canonical load_profile_v1.json so Aditya can match the shape.

What we need from the engineering side for the run:
- Confirm the planned test window (prefer morning PST to match customer team availability)
- Decide whether to run with KV cache warm start (recommended) or cold-start baseline first
- Confirm whether Pioneer wants quantized model variant for cost testing (they asked about 8-bit run)

Aditya — can you own the runbook and coordinate the benchmarking engineers? Priya and Marissa: please review the runbook and confirm resource reservations for a 2-GPU Dedicated slot for the stress window.

Thanks — I'll monitor the meeting and manage customer comms.

Best,
Monica
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pioneer_load_profile_v1.json (attachment), recent-trace-snippets.txt (attachment)

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-pioneer-onboard-artifacts

From: Claire Park <claire.park@pioneerhealth.com>

Date: 2026-12-01T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Handoff: Pioneer Health benchmark goals and initial artifacts

Thanks Monica — that plan works for us. A couple of clarifications from Pioneer:
- The 120 QPS target is for the combined text-generation routes we use (summarize + redact). Average tokens per request on our side is ~28 input / ~36 output.
- We prefer to see a cold-start baseline first, then a warm-start run (KV primed) so we can understand cache benefits.
- For cost analysis, please include a run with the 8-bit quantized variant if that's a supported option (we understand quality may differ).

Proposed window: 2026-12-02 09:00–11:00 PST (we can extend if you want a longer steady-state).

Samir attached the harness and a short script that drives our production-like sequence mix — filename: pioneer_harness_v0.py

Claire
Director of Integrations
Pioneer Health

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Park <claire.park@pioneerhealth.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@pioneerhealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T14:25:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Handoff: Pioneer Health benchmark goals and initial artifacts

Team — outlining the benchmark runbook and checklist so we’re aligned. I uploaded a PDF runbook (redwood_onboard-benchmark-runbook_v1.pdf) to the shared folder and attached the key checklist below. Please review and confirm by EOD so we can lock the 12/02 window.

Runbook highlights / checklist:
1) Pre-run (24 hours)
   - Reserve 2x A100 GPUs in Dedicated (tag: pioneer-DEMO).
   - Ensure model image with quantized and full-precision variants is available on the cluster.
   - Validate autoscaler min=1 max=4; steady target concurrency mapping = 120 QPS.
   - Warm-up dataset: run 3 ramp waves at 25%, 50%, 75% intensity with sample golden_set_small.json.
2) Cold-start baseline (30 minutes)
   - Start from a freshly restarted service; no cache priming. Collect per-request latencies with tracing enabled.
3) Warm-start steady-state (30 minutes)
   - Prime KV cache using the first 10k requests from the harness, then run the 30-minute steady window targeting 120 QPS.
4) Quantized vs FP comparison
   - Run identical steady-state for quantized model; capture token-level differences for 500 samples from golden set.
5) Post-run artifact collection
   - Export telemetry: p95/p99, error rates, CPU/GPU utilization, tail-latency histograms, admission reject counts due to batching.
   - Share raw traces and the consolidated CSV (load_results_20261130.csv) to the Drive folder.

Open questions / blockers:
- Priya: can you confirm whether we should enable the new batching window optimization (experimental)? It reduces latency variance but can change tail behavior.
- Marissa: confirm the Dedicated reservation tick and whether we need capacity engineering on-call during the run.

Customer asks to start at 09:00 PST 12/02 — I’ve booked a tentative slot. If we’re green, I’ll send the calendar invite to Pioneer and the SRE rotation.

Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Onboarding
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_onboard-benchmark-runbook_v1.pdf (attachment)
Related links: https://hubspot.redwood.company/deals/DEAL-8892

From: Claire Park <claire.park@pioneerhealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@pioneerhealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Handoff: Pioneer Health benchmark goals and initial artifacts

Aditya / Monica — thanks for running the two-stage benchmark and sharing artifacts. Quick summary from Pioneer’s side:
- Cold baseline p95 = 640ms (expected), cold p99 spikes to ~1.2s during the first 10 minutes.
- Warm steady-state p95 = 220ms, p99 = 310ms, sustained 122 QPS with <1% errors.
- Quantized run: p95 increases to 260ms and we observed 0.7% token-delta above tolerance on the golden set.

We’re happy to accept the warm steady-state as meeting the SLA (p95 <= 250ms). We requested the raw CSV and the trace bundle; received load_results_20261130.csv and the runbook PDF.

Next steps per Pioneer:
- Move to a staged cutover with 5% traffic to Redwood for two days, then 25%.
- Follow-on item: a small regression check on 1k samples after the first week in production; Claire will follow up on timing.

Appreciate the clear runbook and the quantization comparison — that helped our procurement committee finalize the cost/quality trade-off.

Claire Park
Director of Integrations
Pioneer Health

Attachments: load_results_20261130.csv (attachment)
